packages.name: sqs
packages.doc:
Package sqs is a core/data/queue Broker over Amazon SQS (ADR 0054's deferred
connector, ADR 0211). It lives in the third-party/aws module beside the s3
and cloudwatch writers, so it costs a consumer no vendor the module did not
already carry (ADR 0157).

# Mapping

Publish is SendMessage: the payload base64-encoded in the body, since an
SQS body is text, and the enqueue instant, read from Config.Clock, carried
as a message attribute; the MessageId is the message's ID. Receive is one
ReceiveMessage of at most MaxReceiveBatch messages, its VisibilityTimeout
the policy's rounded up to the second and its WaitTimeSeconds
Config.WaitTime: long polling is the wait, so the broker has no Waker.
Deliveries is ApproximateReceiveCount. Ack is DeleteMessage; Nack is
ChangeMessageVisibility to the retry delay, or, once the message has been
delivered MaxDeliveries times, a SendMessage to the dead-letter queue with
its cause followed by a DeleteMessage — two requests, so a crash between
them dead-letters the message twice and never loses it. A message whose
leases all lapsed is dead-lettered by the Receive that finds it past its
budget, its Reason LEASE_EXPIRED.

# Whose clock is the lease

SQS keeps the visibility timeout on its own clock and to the second, and a
DeleteMessage with an old receipt handle may succeed. The broker therefore
reads Config.Clock before each ReceiveMessage, so the deadline it hands out
never falls after the one SQS keeps, writes it into the receipt, and
refuses an Ack, Nack, Extend or Reject at or past it with
core/data/queue.LeaseExpired, LeaseLost in its trail, before anything is
sent: a consumer that lost its lease learns it, whatever SQS would have
done. The deadline is only as true as the two clocks agree. A receipt is
good with the broker that issued it, whose table holds the receipt handle
and the payload a dead letter needs; one minted by another broker is
core/data/queue.UnknownReceipt, and a renewal voids the receipt it
replaces.

# Capabilities

LeaseExtender (ChangeMessageVisibility), Rejecter (dead-lettered at once),
DelayedNacker (up to MaxVisibility), DelayedPublisher (DelaySeconds, up to
MaxPublishDelay) and DeadLetterReader (a ReceiveMessage on the dead-letter
queue with a zero visibility timeout, which hides nothing; SQS samples a
standard queue, so a listing longer than a page may miss one). Not
Releaser: SQS cannot give back a receive count. Not OncePublisher: SQS
deduplicates on FIFO queues only, which ADR 0054 defers with per-key
ordering. Not Waker: long polling is the wait. Every failed request is the
package's sentinel, core/data/queue.QueueBackendFailed in its trail.

packages.name: s3
packages.doc:
Package s3 is a core/data/vfs FullFS over one S3 bucket, or one prefix of it
(ADR 0056's port, ADR 0211). It lives in the third-party/aws module beside
the s3 logger writer, on the vendor the module already carries (ADR 0157).

# The mapping

A file is an object whose key is Config.Prefix joined with its name; a
directory is a zero-byte marker object whose key ends in a slash, written
by MkdirAll, or any prefix that some key extends. Open, Stat and ReadFile
are HeadObject and GetObject; ReadDir is ListObjectsV2 with the slash
delimiter, paged by Config.MaxKeys; WriteFile and WriteAtomic are one
PutObject; Remove is DeleteObject, refused on a directory that still holds
something; RemoveAll is a paged DeleteObjects.

# Atomic publication without a rename

A PutObject is atomic per key: a reader sees the complete old object or the
complete new one, never a part, and a failed PutObject leaves the old one in
place. That is exactly AtomicWriter's contract, so WriteAtomic is the same
request as WriteFile; the port has no Rename, and none is faked. The two
differ in their mode only: WriteFile keeps the mode of the file it
rewrites, WriteAtomic records perm on every publication.

# What S3 does not have

Modes are recorded as object metadata (ModeMetadata) and reported by Stat;
S3 enforces none of them. Durability is S3's: a PutObject that returned is
stored. ModTime is the object's Last-Modified, to the second. A missing
parent is refused as on disk, so a directory exists only once MkdirAll, or
a write beneath it by another client, made it. Every call is bounded by
Config.Timeout, since the port's methods take no context.

packages.name: cloudwatch
packages.doc:
Package cloudwatch — the AWS adapter. This file (with cred_adapter.go) is the
ONLY place that imports the AWS SDK; every other file is SDK-free and unit-
tested through the deliverFunc seam. The live PutLogEvents lives in an
anonymous closure returned by newDeliverFunc.

Package cloudwatch — range 0.3.25.* (ADR 0015 writer registry; PP octet 0x19).

Package cloudwatch — bridges writer.CredentialProvider onto the AWS SDK's
aws.CredentialsProvider so credentials refresh on each Retrieve. Split from
client.go to keep one struct per file.

Package cloudwatch registers the "cloudwatch" writer factory. It lives under
third-party/ — NOT in pkg/v1 — in the third-party/aws module it shares with
the s3 writer, so the AWS SDK it pulls never enters the module graph of
pkg/v1 consumers (ADR 0012), and a consumer of this writer inherits no other
vendor (ADR 0157).
Blank-importing the package self-registers the factory (and pulls the AWS
SDK), so writer.Open("cloudwatch",
logger.CloudWatchConfig{…}) resolves only in builds that opt in. The factory
wraps the batching terminal sink (cwsink.go) with async (non-blocking ring +
OnDrop) and levelgate (per-writer MinLevel).

Package cloudwatch — the batching terminal Sink. AWS-free: it talks to
CloudWatch Logs only through the deliverFunc seam, so the batching/flush logic
is unit-tested with a fake (the real AWS adapter lives in client.go). Each
record becomes one log event (carrying its RecordEvent.Time); events are
coalesced via the generic kernel batcher and delivered when the batch reaches
the event cap, on the FlushEvery ticker, or on Flush / Close. The
PutLogEvents chronological-order requirement is honoured by the deliver
closure (a stable sort by timestamp), so the coalescing/flush/ticker
machinery is the shared kernel/concur/batcher (ADR 0014), not a hand-rolled copy.

Package cloudwatch — declares the sentinels returned by the CloudWatch writer.
Each var's name equals its errs.Define Reason in SCREAMING_SNAKE form.

packages.name: s3
packages.doc:
Package s3 — the AWS adapter. This file (with cred_adapter.go) is the ONLY
place that imports the AWS SDK; every other file is SDK-free and unit-tested
through the uploadFunc seam. The live PutObject lives in an anonymous closure
returned by newUploadFunc — confining the SDK here and keeping the batching
logic testable without a network.

Package s3 — range 0.3.35.* (ADR 0015 service slot 0x23).

Package s3 — bridges the SDK's writer.CredentialProvider onto the AWS SDK's
aws.CredentialsProvider so credentials refresh on each Retrieve. Split from
client.go to keep one struct per file.

Package s3 — declares the sentinels returned by the S3 writer. Each var's
name equals its errs.Define Reason in SCREAMING_SNAKE form.

Package s3 registers the "s3" writer factory. It lives under third-party/ —
NOT in pkg/v1 — in the third-party/aws module it shares with the cloudwatch
writer, so the AWS SDK it pulls never enters the module graph of pkg/v1
consumers (nothing in the SDK requires that module; see ADR 0012), and a
consumer of this writer inherits no other vendor (ADR 0157).
Blank-importing the package self-registers the factory
(and pulls the AWS SDK), so writer.Open("s3", logger.S3Config{…}) resolves
only in builds that opt in. The factory wraps the batching terminal sink
(s3sink.go) with the async middleware for a non-blocking ring + OnDrop, and
with levelgate for the per-writer MinLevel.

Package s3 — the batching terminal Sink. AWS-free: it talks to S3 only through
the uploader seam, so the batching/flush logic is unit-tested with a fake
(the real AWS adapter lives in client.go). Records are coalesced into one
uploaded object per batch via the generic kernel batcher — flushed when the
buffered bytes reach MaxBatchBytes, on the FlushEvery ticker, or on Flush /
Close. The per-batch object key and the byte-weight both ride in the deliver
closure / WeightOf, so the coalescing/flush/ticker machinery is the shared
kernel/concur/batcher (ADR 0014), not a hand-rolled copy.

symbols.name: AckFailed

code.public: The queue could not settle the message

symbols.doc:
AckFailed wraps a DeleteMessage or ChangeMessageVisibility failure on a
lease that still held; the message stays leased until its deadline.

symbols.name: BatchTooLarge

code.public: The receive batch is larger than SQS allows

symbols.doc: BatchTooLarge refuses a Receive asking for more than MaxReceiveBatch messages.

symbols.name: CodeSQSAckFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeSQSAckFailed identifies a DeleteMessage or ChangeMessageVisibility SQS
refused or never answered for a receipt whose lease still held.

symbols.name: CodeSQSBatchTooLarge
symbols.doc:
CodeSQSBatchTooLarge identifies a Receive asking for more than ten
messages, the most one ReceiveMessage returns.

symbols.name: CodeSQSDelayTooLong
symbols.doc:
CodeSQSDelayTooLong identifies a delay SQS cannot carry: a publication
later than fifteen minutes (DelaySeconds), or a hand-back or a renewal
later than twelve hours (ChangeMessageVisibility).

symbols.name: CodeSQSLeaseLost
symbols.doc:
CodeSQSLeaseLost identifies a receipt whose lease lapsed on the broker's
clock before the call: SQS may already have handed the message to another
consumer, and nothing is sent.

symbols.name: CodeSQSMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
CodeSQSMisconfigured identifies a Config New refuses before any request:
a missing queue URL, region or credentials, a policy the broker cannot
honour on SQS, a long-poll wait above twenty seconds.

symbols.name: CodeSQSReceiveFailed
symbols.doc: CodeSQSReceiveFailed identifies a ReceiveMessage SQS refused or never answered.

symbols.name: CodeSQSSendFailed
symbols.doc: CodeSQSSendFailed identifies a SendMessage SQS refused or never answered.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.spelled: struct{QueueURL string; DeadLetterQueueURL string; Region string; Endpoint string; Credentials writer.CredentialProvider; Clock clock.Clock; Policy corequeue.PolicyValue; WaitTime time.Duration}
symbols.canonical: struct{QueueURL string; DeadLetterQueueURL string; Region string; Endpoint string; Credentials github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/logger/writer.CredentialProvider; Clock github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/clock.Clock; Policy github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/queue.PolicyValue; WaitTime time.Duration}

fields.name: QueueURL
fields.doc: QueueURL is the queue's URL, as GetQueueUrl returns it. Required.

fields.name: DeadLetterQueueURL
fields.doc:
DeadLetterQueueURL is the queue a message is moved to with its cause
once it has been delivered Policy.MaxDeliveries times, or rejected.
Required: the broker owns the decision to dead-letter (ADR 0054), and
a Nack on a last attempt with nowhere to go would lose the message.
The source queue's own redrive policy, if any, should allow more
receives than MaxDeliveries, so SQS never moves a message first.

fields.name: Region
fields.doc: Region is the AWS region of both queues. Required.

fields.name: Endpoint
fields.doc:
Endpoint overrides the SQS endpoint — LocalStack, ElasticMQ, a VPC
endpoint. Empty means the region's.

fields.name: Credentials
fields.doc:
Credentials signs every request, re-read on each signature so a
rotation is picked up. Required: the default credential chain is not
wired, as for the writers.

fields.name: Clock
fields.doc:
Clock stamps the enqueue instant and the lease deadlines a receipt
carries, and judges them. Nil means clock.System.

fields.name: Policy
fields.doc:
Policy is the delivery discipline. Its zero value is refused, as for
every broker; its VisibilityTimeout and its retry ceiling must also
fit MaxVisibility.

fields.name: WaitTime
fields.doc:
WaitTime is how long one Receive long-polls an empty queue before it
returns no message: 0 answers at once, at most MaxWaitTime.

symbols.doc:
Config configures New: the queue, its dead-letter queue, how to reach
them, and the delivery discipline the broker enforces.

symbols.name: DelayTooLong

code.public: The requested delay is longer than SQS allows

symbols.doc: DelayTooLong refuses a delay SQS cannot record; nothing moved.

symbols.name: LeaseLost

code.public: The message lease had already lapsed

symbols.doc:
LeaseLost is the trail code of core/data/queue.LeaseExpired on this
broker: the receipt's deadline, on the broker's clock, had passed.

symbols.name: MaxPayloadBytes
symbols.doc:
MaxPayloadBytes is the largest payload Publish sends: 191 KiB, which
base64 and the broker's attributes keep under the 256 KiB an SQS
message has carried since the service began, and every emulator
accepts. A Policy.MaxMessageBytes above it is lowered to it, and a
larger payload is core/data/queue.MessageTooLarge.

symbols.name: MaxPublishDelay
symbols.doc:
MaxPublishDelay is the latest a delayed publication may become receivable
(DelaySeconds 900).

symbols.name: MaxReceiveBatch
symbols.doc:
MaxReceiveBatch is the most messages one Receive leases: ReceiveMessage's
MaxNumberOfMessages ceiling. A larger max is refused with BatchTooLarge
rather than clamped, so a consumer configured for more learns it at once.

symbols.name: MaxVisibility
symbols.doc:
MaxVisibility is the longest lease, retry delay or renewal SQS records
(VisibilityTimeout 43200 s). A policy whose VisibilityTimeout or retry
ceiling is longer is refused at New.

symbols.name: MaxWaitTime
symbols.doc: MaxWaitTime is the longest long poll SQS accepts (WaitTimeSeconds 20).

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a broker over the SQS queue at cfg.QueueURL. It sends no
request: everything decidable without SQS is decided here, and a refusal
is SQSMisconfigured or core/data/queue.QueueMisconfigured.

symbols.name: ReceiveFailed

code.public: The queue could not be read

symbols.doc: ReceiveFailed wraps a ReceiveMessage failure; nothing was leased.

symbols.name: SQSMisconfigured

code.public: The SQS queue broker is misconfigured

symbols.doc: SQSMisconfigured refuses a Config New cannot build a broker from.

symbols.name: SendFailed

code.public: The queue could not accept the message

symbols.doc: SendFailed wraps a SendMessage failure; nothing was published.

symbols.name: AccessDenied

code.public: Access to the storage bucket was denied

symbols.doc: AccessDenied reports a request the credentials may not make.

symbols.name: BucketMissing

code.public: The storage bucket does not exist

symbols.doc: BucketMissing reports a bucket S3 does not know.

symbols.name: CodeS3FSAccessDenied
symbols.doc: CodeS3FSAccessDenied identifies a request the credentials are not allowed to make (403).

symbols.name: CodeS3FSBucketMissing
symbols.doc: CodeS3FSBucketMissing identifies a request on a bucket S3 does not know (NoSuchBucket).

symbols.name: CodeS3FSMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
CodeS3FSMisconfigured identifies a Config New refuses before any request:
a missing bucket, region or credentials, a prefix that is not a clean
relative path, a page size outside 1..1000, a non-positive timeout.

symbols.name: CodeS3FSObjectTooLarge
symbols.doc:
CodeS3FSObjectTooLarge identifies a write above MaxObjectBytes, the most
one PutObject carries; multipart upload is out of scope.

symbols.name: CodeS3FSRequestFailed
symbols.doc: CodeS3FSRequestFailed identifies any other S3 failure, the cause kept in the chain.

symbols.name: CodeS3FSThrottled
symbols.doc: CodeS3FSThrottled identifies a request S3 slowed down (SlowDown, 503).

symbols.name: Config
symbols.spelled: struct{Bucket string; Prefix string; Region string; Endpoint string; Credentials writer.CredentialProvider; MaxKeys int32; Timeout time.Duration}
symbols.canonical: struct{Bucket string; Prefix string; Region string; Endpoint string; Credentials github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/logger/writer.CredentialProvider; MaxKeys int32; Timeout time.Duration}

fields.name: Bucket
fields.doc: Bucket is the bucket's name. Required.

fields.name: Prefix
fields.doc:
Prefix roots the filesystem under a key prefix: "assets" makes the name
"a.txt" the key "assets/a.txt". Empty roots it at the bucket. It must be
a clean relative path (io/fs.ValidPath), "." excepted.

fields.name: Region
fields.doc: Region is the bucket's AWS region. Required.

fields.name: Endpoint
fields.doc:
Endpoint overrides the S3 endpoint, in path style — LocalStack, MinIO,
any S3-compatible store. Empty means the region's.

fields.name: Credentials
fields.doc:
Credentials signs every request, re-read on each signature. Required,
as for the s3 writer.

fields.name: MaxKeys
fields.doc:
MaxKeys is how many keys one ListObjectsV2 page asks for, 1 to 1000; a
listing larger than a page is read page by page. Zero is refused
rather than defaulted (ADR 0031).

fields.name: Timeout
fields.doc:
Timeout bounds every request, since the port's methods take no
context. Zero is refused: its two readings, "no bound" and "fail at
once", are opposites (ADR 0031).

symbols.doc:
Config configures New: the bucket and prefix the filesystem is rooted at,
how to reach them, and the bounds every call keeps.

symbols.name: MaxObjectBytes
symbols.doc:
MaxObjectBytes is the largest file WriteFile and WriteAtomic publish: the
single-PutObject limit, 5 GiB.

symbols.name: ModeMetadata
symbols.doc:
ModeMetadata is the user-metadata key a file's or a directory's
permission bits are recorded under, in octal (x-amz-meta-mode).

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns the filesystem rooted at cfg.Prefix in cfg.Bucket. It sends no
request: a missing bucket is BucketMissing on the first call that reaches
it.

symbols.name: ObjectTooLarge

code.public: The file is too large to store

symbols.doc: ObjectTooLarge refuses a write above MaxObjectBytes; nothing was sent.

symbols.name: RequestFailed
symbols.doc: RequestFailed wraps any other S3 failure.

symbols.name: S3FSMisconfigured
symbols.doc: S3FSMisconfigured refuses a Config New cannot build a filesystem from.

symbols.name: Throttled

code.public: The storage service is throttling requests

symbols.doc: Throttled reports a request S3 slowed down; retrying later may succeed.

symbols.name: ClientInitFailed

code.public: CloudWatch writer could not initialise its AWS client

symbols.doc:
ClientInitFailed wraps an AWS SDK client construction failure at Open
time (bad region, unreachable credential source, …).

symbols.name: CodeCWClientInitFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeCWClientInitFailed identifies a failure building the AWS CloudWatch Logs
client from the supplied region / credentials at Open time.

symbols.name: CodeCWEventRejected
symbols.doc:
CodeCWEventRejected identifies a single event dropped before delivery because
its timestamp falls outside the PutLogEvents per-event bounds (older than 14
days or more than 2 hours in the future). The event is dropped and surfaced
via OnError instead of failing the whole batch.

symbols.name: CodeCWPutFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeCWPutFailed identifies a failed PutLogEvents delivery of a batched set of
log events.

symbols.name: EventRejected

code.public: CloudWatch writer dropped a log event with an out-of-range timestamp

symbols.doc:
EventRejected reports one event dropped before delivery because its
timestamp is outside the PutLogEvents per-event window (older than 14 days
or more than 2 hours ahead). The whole batch still ships; only the
out-of-window event is discarded and routed to OnError.

symbols.name: PutFailed

code.public: CloudWatch writer failed to deliver a log batch

symbols.doc: PutFailed wraps a failed PutLogEvents delivery of a batch.

symbols.name: Writer
symbols.doc: Writer is the registered cloudwatch factory singleton (no init()).

symbols.name: ClientInitFailed

code.public: S3 writer could not initialise its AWS client

symbols.doc:
ClientInitFailed wraps an AWS SDK config/client construction failure at
Open time (bad region, unreachable credential source, …).

symbols.name: CodeS3ClientInitFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeS3ClientInitFailed identifies a failure building the AWS S3 client from
the supplied region / credentials at Open time.

symbols.name: CodeS3PutFailed
symbols.doc: CodeS3PutFailed identifies a failed PutObject upload of a batched log object.

symbols.name: PutFailed

code.public: S3 writer failed to upload a log batch

symbols.doc: PutFailed wraps a failed PutObject upload of a batched log object.

symbols.name: Writer
symbols.doc: Writer is the registered s3 factory singleton (no init(); package-level var).
